purpose: Differentiate Lesson7–12 neighborhood from unchanged Lesson1–6 garden while retaining original characters and the single-world layout

calls.reason: Visible horizontal composition break between the upper street and the middle alley
calls.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. A production environment asset for the second chapter of a children's English learning journey.

Image 1 is a STYLE-ONLY reference for the already approved first chapter. Keep its warm cream limestone, muted coral walls, terracotta roofs, teal accents, soft green plants, upper-left sunlight, rounded storybook rendering and friendly three-quarter perspective. DO NOT copy its landform, canal layout, three round terraces, S-shaped bridges or building positions. Image 2 is an EXISTING CHARACTER STYLE/SCALE reference only; do not draw any people or lesson props.

Create a clearly DIFFERENT place: a lived-in NEIGHBORHOOD TOWN STREET. One unified tall 1:3 composition, ideally 1024x3072. Most of the scene is connected street-level paving and two-story homes with porches, balconies, shutters, small awnings, potted plants, garden fences and a modest school entrance. Use predominantly angular/chamfered street corners and broad rectangular forecourts, rather than three semicircular elevated garden platforms. A pedestrian street continues from top to bottom, gently changing direction through the neighborhood; short architectural steps can occur only outside the standing zones. Buildings provide enclosure and spatial rhythm. Water is absent or at most a tiny distant detail, never an open canal running down the image. No giant arches supporting repeated platforms, no floating islands, no maze of layered bridges.

This image is one consistent camera/scale, not three separate panels. It will be shown in three contiguous square sections. Preserve THREE specific quiet, level stone standing areas needed for unchanged character overlays: in EACH square, local x=20%-80%, y=42%-64% is unobstructed level pavement, with feet at local(50%,56%). Globally the foot points are at about (50%,18.67%), (50%,52%), (50%,85.33%). Keep the middle lower band of EACH square (x=28%-72%, local y=58%-84%) simple warm cream paving for separately rendered stars/lesson controls, without a step edge, chair, bush, doorway, post or dark contrast there. The central standing zones must feel like natural widenings of the continuous street, not plinths.
Buildings may be large enough to recognize but should stay mainly toward the sides and upper/back areas of each square, never blocking the standing zones.

Top square, Lesson7-8 conversation: a welcoming house-front street with a recessed porch, teal shutters, a modest small awning and an off-center bench along a wall. No flower arch identical to chapter1. Center is open street pavement.
Middle square, Lesson9-10 greeting: a distinct corner where two neighborhood facades meet, with rounded-corner low walls, side doorsteps and window flower boxes; a wide chamfered rectangular junction in the center. Keep lamp posts at the outside edges.
Bottom square, Lesson11-12 lost-property school: a rectangular school entrance forecourt, modest cream building with terracotta roof and teal double doors toward the rear LEFT or across the back, side picket fence and a small tree; a broad level forecourt in the center. Do not reuse the same right-side school composition from chapter1.

Match the approved art style closely, while making the street/town identity unmistakable at phone size. Calm, warm and sunny. Fewer repeated flowers and cypress cones than chapter1; use a mix of potted greenery, small deciduous trees and domestic details. One geographically plausible walking route, coherent walls and ground heights.
No figures, animals, handbag, umbrella, shirt, text, numbers, logos, signs with writing, pins, stars, medals, UI, cards, section borders, watermarks, collage seams or dramatic bloom. Finished opaque image.

calls.reason: Street transition remained spatially ambiguous; native image also was 724x2171 rather than exact 1:3
calls.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
This is an EDIT of the supplied neighborhood-town illustration. Keep the SAME 1:3 dimensions, cream/coral/teal/terracotta palette, sunny soft storybook rendering, homes, porches, trees, bench, awnings and school theme. Keep the large clear paved standing areas near whole-image (50%,18.7%), (50%,52%), (50%,85.3%) unobstructed and in place. Do not add people or UI.

Fix ONE major flaw: the scene currently has a visible horizontal collage-like cut at roughly one-third of the image height. The upper foreground pavement abruptly ends above a newly starting distant alley, as if separate pictures were stacked. Remove that discontinuity and the repeated horizon/camera restart. Reconstruct this transition as a physically coherent, continuous neighborhood lane with a natural angled turn and, if necessary, a short visible stair connection at the SIDE. Ground heights and building foundations must make sense; road surfaces must actually meet. No exposed horizontal seam, strip boundary, pasted roof edge, floating slab or unreachable walkway. Maintain one consistent oblique camera and masonry scale across the entire tall image. Also ensure the lower transition into the school forecourt reads as the same continuous street, with no abrupt panel reset.
The result is ONE long connected urban scene, never three panels. Retain the distinct urban arrangement and very little/no water; do not revert to garden islands, repeated semicircular terraces or S bridges. Preserve the clear central paving around all three existing standing zones, and keep decorative objects at the sides. No words, numbers, logos, stars, medals, markers, people or generated characters.

Create ONE uninterrupted isometric neighborhood street, tall portrait with exact 1:3 canvas ratio (for example 724x2172, or1024x3072; height exactly three times width).
Reference image1 supplies ONLY the approved cream/coral/teal colors, soft warm storybook rendering and sunshine. Reference image2 supplies ONLY the domestic facade design language (porches, shutters, awnings). Do not reuse either reference's layout.

CRITICAL GEOGRAPHY: use a single continuous gently bending boulevard at ONE ground level, seen in consistent PARALLEL/isometric projection. The light cream paved street occupies the central half of the entire image, from the very top through the middle to the bottom. The viewer must be able to trace the same unbroken paved surface all the way down. Houses and trees form the sides of the street, never a roof or cliff laid across it. NO horizontal cuts, NO new distant horizon halfway down, NO stacked pictures, NO discontinuous elevated platforms, NO S-shaped bridges, NO repeated round plazas, NO water canals. A very small bend or junction is fine, but never an unconnected second street.

Architecture: welcoming two-storey cream and coral neighborhood houses on both sides, terracotta roofs, teal shutters and doors, small front porches, side benches, window boxes, a few awnings and trees. Domestic street life is implied by architecture only; no people. Near the upper RIGHT edge use an inviting front porch and a bench. Around the middle LEFT/RIGHT edges use a chamfered corner house and a striped awning to distinguish the greeting junction. Near the lower LEFT edge include a modest school facade with teal double doors and a side fence. Place these landmarks alongside the same road, not in separate panels. All buildings have consistent human-scale doors and masonry. Upper-left warm sunlight, restrained soft contact shadows. Warm and spacious; green planting remains at the side edges. Minimal/no blue water.

UNOBSTRUCTED CONTACT AREAS: keep broad, flat, simple paving across x20%-80% in the following global vertical ranges: y14%-22%, y47%-55%, y80%-88%. The existing characters will stand at (50%,18.67%), (50%,52%), (50%,85.33%); do not draw them. These are points on the SAME street. At those positions and just below them, no steps, lamps, furniture, plant beds, wall ends or deep shadows. Keep center x30%-70% visually quiet all the way down for interface labels. Natural simple paving is desired, not blank circles or placeholders.

Match the approved painterly soft-volume children's game aesthetic, while being clearly an urban neighborhood rather than the first chapter's waterside garden. Do not introduce a different palette or photorealism. No text, numbers, logos, people, animals, lesson props, stars, medals, pins, UI or watermarks. Opaque complete finished image.
